主题：约翰·J·霍兰（John J. HOLLAND）向法国当局提出出售7架轰炸机的提议。
参阅：向法国当局提供的战争物资。
1941年3月1日，“美国出口商”（American Exporters）公司的代表约翰·J·霍兰拜访了负责馆务的法国副领事博罗伊（BEAUROY）先生，提议向法属印度支那总督府出售当时位于马尼拉的7架轰炸机。
兹附上我们在快速调查过程中收集到的关于霍兰的某些信息。
约翰·约瑟夫·霍兰（John Joseph HOLLAND），年龄约33岁，系英国臣民（加拿大籍或澳大利亚籍）。他于1938年10月底从香港抵达上海，此前他在香港担任悉尼《每日电讯报》（Daily Telegraph）的通讯员。
档案
1939年，应其妻子鲍里斯（Boris）(?) 艾米丽·穆里尔·霍兰（Emily Muriel HOLLAND）的请求，澳大利亚当局曾对他进行调查，他将妻子抛弃且未留下任何钱财。
当时，国际警察未能发现霍兰在上海的任何踪迹。然而，他们查明他在此地为人所知，且因欠下大量债务，他有充分的理由躲藏。他未在

ernment/Indo-China 7 bombers which at that time

Herewith follows certain information

John Joseph HOLLAND, aged about 33 years,
is a British subject (Canadian or Australian). He
arrived in Shanghai from Hong Kong, where he worked
as correspondent to the "Daily Telegraph" (Sydney),
at the end of October, 1938.

In 1939 the Australian Authorities were
making enquiries about him at the request of his
wife Boris (?) Emily Muriel HOLLAND whom he had
abandoned without any money.

The International Police were not able
to find any trace of HOLLAND in Shanghai at that
time. They established, however, that he was known
in this city and as he had contracted numerous debts,
he had good reasons to hide. He was not registered

秘密

译文

报告

1941年3月5日。

第 5589/S 号

主题：约翰·J·霍兰（John J. HOLLAND）向法国当局提出出售7架轰炸机的提议。

参阅：向法国当局提供的战争物资。

1941年3月1日，“美国出口商”（American Exporters）公司的代表约翰·J·霍兰拜访了负责馆务的法国副领事博罗伊（BEAUROY）先生，提议向法属印度支那总督府出售当时位于马尼拉的7架轰炸机。

兹附上我们在快速调查过程中收集到的关于霍兰的某些信息。

约翰·约瑟夫·霍兰（John Joseph HOLLAND），年龄约33岁，系英国臣民（加拿大籍或澳大利亚籍）。他于1938年10月底从香港抵达上海，此前他在香港担任悉尼《每日电讯报》（Daily Telegraph）的通讯员。

1939年，应其妻子鲍里斯（Boris）(?) 艾米丽·穆里尔·霍兰（Emily Muriel HOLLAND）的请求，澳大利亚当局曾对他进行调查，他将妻子抛弃且未留下任何钱财。

当时，国际警察未能发现霍兰在上海的任何踪迹。然而，他们查明他在此地为人所知，且因欠下大量债务，他有充分的理由躲藏。他未在

pages.en:
- 2 -

at the British Consulate-General.

He now works in the firm "American
Exporters" which has a doubtful reputation in
local commercial circles. The Manager of this
firm, an American Jew named RAISIN, is strongly
suspected of dealing in contraband arms; he is
otherwise known for his relations with the Japanese.
Moreover, this firm included amongst its employees,
or rather "collaborators" people such as ECKELMAN,
alias Carl LUND, German, notable swindler; and
JECHIVI, alias ASHBY, alias Captain BERTRAND, French
of Algerian extraction, also well known to our Police
as an international swindler.

HOLLAND now lives at No. 230A Route de
Boissezon, Tel:77443. This house is registered
with the Revenue Office of the French Municipality
under the name of Mr. A.W. RAYMOND, employed in
"Edgar & Co", 18 The Bund, Tel:13535.

We are not aware if it is really true
that the firm "American Exporters" is preparing
to sell war aeroplanes. Nevertheless, it is not
unlikely that HOLLAND made such a proposal with
the object of provocation, especially when the
"special" relations with the Japanese of the Manager
of the firm on whose behalf he is acting, are taken
into account.

JM.

CONFIDENTIAL

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No: ......
No. S. B. D. ......
S. 1, Special Branch Station
REPORT
Date November 26, 1939.

Subject John Joseph HOLLAND.

Made by. D.P.S. Killingbeck Forwarded by. C. G. ......

With reference to the attached enquiry from H.B.M.
Consulate-General, concerning John Joseph HOLLAND,
enquiries made at all likely places have failed to
reveal any trace of the present whereabouts of this
person.

Records on file in C.S.6 show that Holland
resided at 458 Szechuen Road for a short period, but
left that address on February 7, 1938, since which
time there is no trace of his movements. Various
personalities in newspaper circles remember Holland,
but as he does not appear to have been employed by any
newspaper office in Shanghai, they are unable to supply
any information that would help to locate him.

Holland is alleged to have been heavily in debt
in Shanghai at the time he left his lodgings in
Szechuen Road and his board and lodging at that address
still remain unpaid. He was vouched for by another
resident at the same address, a Mr. W.V.D. White, of
the China Journal Publishing Company, 117 Hong Kong Road,
but as this person has left Shanghai, presumably for
Australia, no information is forthcoming from that source.

In view of the abovementioned facts concerning
Holland's financial standing and the fact that he has
not registered himself at H.B.M. Consulate-General, it
would appear that Holland has every intention of keeping
his whereabouts from being generally known.

Killingbeck
D. P. S.

D. C. (Special Branch).

报告
日期：1939年11月26日。

事由：约翰·约瑟夫·霍兰（HOLLAND）。

制作人：D.P.S. 基林贝克（Killingbeck） 转呈人：C. G. ......

关于附上的英国总领事馆就约翰·约瑟夫·霍兰一事提出的查询，经在所有可能的地点进行调查，未能发现此人目前下落的任何线索。

中央搜查课6组（C.S.6）的存档记录显示，霍兰曾在四川路458号短期居住，但于1938年2月7日离开该地址，此后便无其行踪的记录。新闻界的几位人士记得霍兰，但由于他似乎未曾受雇于上海的任何报社，他们无法提供有助于定位他的任何信息。

据称，霍兰在离开四川路的住所时在上海负债累累，他在该地址的食宿费用至今仍未支付。当时同住的另一位居民，即香港路117号《中国评论》出版公司（China Journal Publishing Company）的W.V.D.怀特（White）先生曾为他作保，但由于此人已离开上海，推测是前往澳大利亚，因此无法从该来源获得任何信息。

鉴于上述关于霍兰财务状况的事实，以及他未在英國總領事館登記的事實，霍兰似乎有意不让他人知晓其下落。

基林贝克
副巡官（D. P. S.）

特科副督察（D. C.）。

New South Wales.

22nd May, 1939.

Sir,

I have the honour, at the instance of Ministers,
to transmit herewith in accordance with the provisions of
Section 5 of the Maintenance Orders (Facilities for
Enforcement) Act, 1923, the undermentioned documents with
reference to a provisional Maintenance Order made against
one John Joseph Holland, on the complaint of his wife Doris
Emily Muriel Holland, and to request that you will be so
good as to take the necessary steps for confirmation of the
order and its enforcement under the provisions of Ordinance
9 of 1921, Hong Kong:-

1. Complaint
2. Deposition of the complainant
3. Certified copy of the provisional order.
4. Statement of the grounds upon which confirmation
of the order may be opposed.
5. Record of exhibits -
(i) Marriage certificate
(ii) photograph of the defendant.

It is desired that any money paid in satisfaction
of the order be remitted to the Clerk of the Children's
Court, Sydney, New South Wales.

Defendant is said to reside at Hong Kong, and to
be employed as foreign correspondent at Hong Kong for the
Sydney "Daily Telegraph" newspaper and his description is
as follows:-

About 5' 7" in height, mid-brown hair (greyish)
green eyes, medium build, rather sharp features,
very small moustache, between 9 and 9½ stones
weight, straight hair, always well groomed and
31 years of age.

I shall be glad to be informed in due course
whether the order has been confirmed.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your Excellency's most obedient servant,
(Signed) Wakehurst.
Governor.

His Excellency

The Governor of Hongkong.

（副本）。

新南威尔士州。

1939年5月22日。

先生：

奉部长之命，谨根据1923年《赡养费令（执行便利）法》第5条之规定，随函转交下列文件，这些文件涉及因其妻多丽丝·艾米丽·穆里尔·霍兰（Doris Emily Muriel Holland）投诉而针对约翰·约瑟夫·霍兰作出的临时赡养费令，并恳请阁下采取必要步骤，根据1921年香港第9号条例确认该令并予以执行：-

1. 投诉书
2. 投诉人证词
3. 临时令的核证副本。
4. 反对确认该令的理由陈述。
5. 物证记录 -
(i) 结婚证书
(ii) 被告照片。

希望将履行该令所支付的任何款项汇至新南威尔士州悉尼儿童法院书记员处。

据称被告居住在香港，并受雇为悉尼《每日电讯报》（Daily Telegraph）驻香港的外国通讯员，其体貌特征如下：-

身高约5英尺7英寸，中棕色头发（略带灰色），绿色眼睛，中等身材，五官较为犀利，胡须非常稀疏，体重在9至9.5英石之间，直发，总是衣着整洁，年龄31岁。

如蒙告知该令是否已获确认，不胜感激。

谨此致意，
先生，
总督阁下最顺从的仆人，
（签署）韦克赫斯特（Wakehurst）。
总督。

致
香港总督阁下。

Government House,
Hong Kong, 31st July, 1939.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge the receipt of
Your Excellency's letter dated 22nd May, 1939, regarding
a provisional Maintenance Order made against John Joseph
Holland on the complaint of his wife Boris Emily Muriel
Holland, and to inform Your Excellency that Mr. Holland
appears to have left Hong Kong on 31st October, 1938, for
Shanghai, and has not since returned. It has not,
therefore, been possible to take steps to confirm the order
up to now and I propose with Your Excellency's concurrence
to keep the papers enclosed in Your Excellency's letter for
a further six months in case Mr. Holland returns to this
Colony within that time.

I have, &c.,

(Sd.) G. A. S. Northcote.
Governor.

His Excellency
The Governor,
Sydney,
New South Wales,
Australia.

New South Wales.
Government House,
Sydney.
24th August, 1939.

Sir,
Referring to my despatch of the 22nd May, 1939,
and Your Excellency's reply of the 31st July, 1939,
regarding a provisional Maintenance Order made against
John Joseph Holland, on the complaint of his wife Boris
Emily Holland, I have now the honour, at the instance of
Ministers, to inform you that Mrs. Holland states that,
although some difficulty might be experienced in locating
the defendant, enquiries can be made of Miss Jean Findlay,
30 Body Road, Kowloon, who can and will supply information
as to his whereabouts. Mrs. Holland added that she
understands her husband may leave very shortly for England
and requests that the provisional order may be confirmed
at an early date.

I have, &c.,
(Sd.) Wakehurst.
Governor.

His Excellency
The Governor of Hong Kong.

Government House,
Hong Kong, 24th October, 1939.

My Lord,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt of Your
Lordship's letter of 24th August, 1939, regarding a
provisional maintenance order made against John Joseph
Holland on the complaint of his wife Boris Emily Muriel
Holland, and in reply to inform Your Lordship that enquiries
have been made as requested of Miss Jean Findlay, 30 Mody
Road, Kowloon, who states that she has not seen Mr. Holland
since the beginning of 1938, and knows nothing of his
present whereabouts.

I am forwarding copies of this correspondence to
His Majesty's Consul-General, Shanghai, for such action
as he may consider desirable.

I have the honour to be,
My Lord,
Your Lordship's most obedient servant,

Signed: G.A.S. Northcote.
Governor.

The Right Honourable
Lord Wakehurst, K.C.M.G.,
Governor,
Sydney,
New South Wales,
Australia.
